newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage rates rise in week.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage rates rise in week.

text.p: U.S. home mortgage rates rose during the week ending Aug. 8, Freddie Mac said Thursday.

"The good employment news released last Friday helped push interest rates up over last week's figures. Nevertheless, mortgage interest rates are still at a very affordable level," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said.

Thirty-year mortgages rose to an average of 7.46 percent from 7.36 percent last week, while 15-year mortgages increased to an average of 7.00 percent from 6.90 percent the prior week, Freddie Mac reported.
One-year adjustable rate mortgages also inched higher to 5.53 percent from 5.49 percent last week.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.88 percent, the 15-year 7.40 percent and the adjustable mortgage 5.89 percent.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.5 percent on the adjusable loan, up from 1.4 percent the previous week.
Last week the Labour Department reported a 316,000 increase in U.S. July nonfarm payrolls and a jobless rate of 4.8 percent, a report that helped send interest rates higher.
Next week the Labour Department will issue U.S. July producer and consumer prices.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
